_doc: Agents in Situationship — 20 modern-dating scenarios designed as an internet-native behavioral archetype game. Each scenario has 4 lettered options. The judge sums per-trait weights, detects 'disorganized' via 3 consistency probe pairs, and derives a viral archetype label. NO option scores secure>=1 — there is no 'healthy answer' escape hatch. Every option encodes a real dysregulated pattern.
design_principle: Specific, messy, real-world tiny social behaviors. Mix of texting, group dynamics, vulnerability, jealousy, conflict. Many options encode contradictory traits simultaneously (anxious+avoidant). 'Unbothered' weight is always performative (paired with toxic or avoidant) — never the genuinely-healthy escape. Labels surface viral internet personas, not therapy categories.

questions.text: They reposted a celebrity thirst trap at 2am. You both saw it. You're literally in bed next to them.

A.text: Repost an even hotter thirst trap of someone else to your story.

B.text: Bring it up the next morning. 'Just curious.' Tone slightly wrong.

C.text: Watch them watch the next 6 stories. Time how long they linger on each.

D.text: Like it yourself, then turn your back to sleep. Bring it up never.

questions.text: You sent a long voice message last night. They replied 'k' this morning.

A.text: Send another voice note: 'did I say something weird? lol'

B.text: 'k' them back. Make them feel it.

C.text: Send a clarifying paragraph + a meme + an apology no one asked for.

D.text: Pretend you never sent it. Don't reference it again, even when relevant.

questions.text: They cancelled plans night-of. Again. Same vague excuse.

A.text: 'no worries! 💛 maybe next week?' — send detailed proposed plans within 2 hours.

B.text: Read receipt. Don't reply. Plan a 'spontaneous' night out and post it to your story.

C.text: Convince yourself they're going through it. Send flowers via DoorDash.

D.text: Cancel on them next time with the same vague excuse. Don't elaborate.

questions.text: Their friend group is at the bar. You arrive together. Within 20 minutes they're across the room, deep in conversation with someone you don't recognize.

A.text: Drift over and casually slot yourself into the conversation. Smile at the stranger.

B.text: Make a new best friend in the next hour out of spite. Be the loudest at this bar.

C.text: Stand alone at the bar. Refresh their Find My Friends. Watch them not move.

D.text: Leave without telling them. Time how long until they notice.

questions.text: They said 'I miss you' 4 days ago and haven't suggested meeting up since.

A.text: Reply 'miss you more' — then text again the next day with a specific plan.

B.text: Re-read the 'miss you' 12 times. Decide they're seeing someone else. Audit their tagged photos.

C.text: Mention it casually mid-other-conversation, like a test. Watch their response.

D.text: Reply slower. Be a little colder. Don't say why.

questions.text: They have an 'opposite-gender best friend' who's always around. You've never met them.

A.text: Look up the friend's Instagram. Then LinkedIn. Then their ex. Build a dossier.

B.text: Bring up the friend 4 times this week. Gauge their reaction each time.

C.text: Become weirdly close with one of YOUR opposite-gender friends. Post a photo together.

D.text: Pretend you have no opinion. Be subtly distant for a week.

questions.text: They text 'we need to talk' with no other context.

A.text: Reply 'sure, when?' Spiral for 6 hours about possibilities.

B.text: Don't reply for hours. Let them sit with the silence.

C.text: Text three friends. Reply when they confirm 'it's probably nothing.'

D.text: 'About what.' Don't elaborate.

questions.text: You hooked up for the first time last night. They wake up and immediately get on their phone for 15 minutes without speaking.

A.text: Start soft small talk. Smile too much. Make coffee performatively.

B.text: Get on YOUR phone too. Pretend you have somewhere to be.

C.text: Replay every detail of last night. Identify what you did wrong.

D.text: Sigh once. Make it their problem to figure out.

questions.text: They told you they love you. You weren't ready. You said 'thank you' by accident.

A.text: Spend the next 3 days drafting a long heartfelt text to fix it.

B.text: Don't bring it up. Hope they don't either.

C.text: Buy them something expensive within 48 hours. Don't mention the love thing.

D.text: Start saying 'I love you too' reflexively after every interaction. Mean it half.

questions.text: You finally meet their friend group. Their friends are polite but go quiet whenever you join the conversation.

A.text: Try harder. Make a joke. Then another. Then explain the joke.

B.text: Excuse yourself to the bathroom. Stay 12 minutes. Check yourself in the mirror twice.

C.text: Notice. Bring it up in the car on the way home. Tone measured but pointed.

D.text: Get one drink louder. Become the most charming person there by sheer will.

questions.text: They asked what you're looking for.

A.text: Mirror whatever they say. Adjust your needs to fit theirs.

B.text: 'Idk man, just vibing.'

C.text: Give a vague answer to keep options open.

D.text: Over-explain — list your values, your timeline, your fears, your attachment style.

questions.text: You're at their place for the first time. You open the bedside drawer 'looking for a charger.' There's a card from someone you don't know.

A.text: Close the drawer. Pretend you didn't see it. Wonder about it for the next 6 months.

B.text: Take a photo of the front of the card. Save it to a hidden album.

C.text: Bring it up casually next week. Time the question carefully.

D.text: Mention it right now. Watch their face. Note every micro-expression.

questions.text: You're at a party. Their ex walks in.

A.text: Watch your situationship like a hawk all night.

B.text: Leave early. Don't tell them why.

C.text: Bring up the ex on the ride home. Casually. With detail.

D.text: Pretend not to notice. Spend the next week investigating the ex on social media.

questions.text: You see them like a 2019 photo of someone you don't know on Instagram.

A.text: Check that person's entire profile. Their job. Where they live. Who they follow.

B.text: Like an old photo of one of your exes in retaliation.

C.text: Bring it up three days later. Make it sound casual.

D.text: Note this. Be slightly less available for a few days.

questions.text: They corrected you in front of your boss at a work event.

A.text: Laugh it off. Stay extra warm with them the rest of the night to show you're fine.

B.text: Bring it up the moment you're in the car. Voice slightly too high.

C.text: Go quiet for the rest of the event. Be cold in a way that's clearly cold.

D.text: Make a 'joke' at their expense in front of their colleagues two weeks later.

questions.text: You're at brunch. Mid-meal, you see them texting under the table.

A.text: Don't say anything. Excuse yourself. Stay in the bathroom 10 minutes.

B.text: Ask who they're texting. Tone slightly off.

C.text: Pull out your own phone. Text someone — anyone — pretend you have plans.

D.text: Watch their face. Try to read the texts in their eye movement.

questions.text: They got a promotion. You feel a tiny weird thing in your chest you don't admit.

A.text: Post a thirst trap of yourself the same day 'for no reason.'

B.text: Plan a celebration. Be the most enthusiastic person in their life this week. Overcompensate.

C.text: Take 6 extra hours to reply when they share good work news.

D.text: Start aggressively applying for jobs you're not qualified for.

questions.text: They forgot your birthday. They remember two days late and feel awful.

A.text: 'It's fine, don't worry!' Mean it half.

B.text: Accept the apology. Bring it up three weeks later during an unrelated fight.

C.text: 'Yeah.' Don't say anything else.

D.text: Forgive them out loud. Vent in detail to three friends over the next week.

questions.text: You finally tell them what you want from this thing. They reply: 'let's just enjoy this for now.'

A.text: 'Okay, that works for me.' — even though it doesn't.

B.text: Start emotionally pulling away. Reply slower. Get colder.

C.text: Agree. Then convince yourself they'll come around in 3 weeks.

D.text: End it preemptively. Better to leave than be left.

questions.text: It's 2am. They text 'u up?'

A.text: Reply 'yeah, you?' — pretend you weren't waiting.

B.text: Wait 6 hours, then reply 'sorry just saw this.'

C.text: See it. Don't reply. Stare at the screen for 20 minutes.

D.text: Reply right away with a long flirty paragraph — way too long for 2am.
